Derive AOI polygons by buffering point coordinates

mutate_aoi_buffer.Rd

Buffers each valid point row by a given metric distance (after projecting to a planar CRS) and writes a sequential AOI ID back to the data. The per-row buffer polygons are attached as an AOI sf for downstream fetching functions.

Usage

mutate_aoi_buffer(
  df,
  lat = "lat",
  lon = "lon",
  dist = 100,
  .name = "aoi_id",
  crs_planar = 3857
)

Arguments

df

A data frame (or tibble) with point coordinates.

lat, lon

Names (strings or symbols) of the latitude and longitude columns in df. Must be in WGS84 (EPSG:4326).

dist

Buffer radius in meters (applied in a planar CRS).

.name

Name of the output column in df that stores the AOI ID (e.g., "aoi_id"). If a column of the same name exists, it will be overwritten.

crs_planar

EPSG code for the planar (projected) CRS used during buffering. Defaults to Web Mercator (EPSG:3857).

Value

The input df, with a new .name column (character AOI ID) and AOI-related attributes (see Attributes).

Details

  • Coordinates are validated; rows with non-finite lat/lon get NA in the ID column and no polygon is produced for them.

  • The function preserves row order and does not reshuffle df.

  • One AOI polygon is produced per valid input row (not deduplicated).

  • Buffering is performed in crs_planar, then geometries are transformed back to WGS84 and run through sf::st_make_valid().

  • AOI IDs are sequential strings (e.g., "aoi_001").

  • A standard set of attributes is written to df for sibling functions.

Attributes

  • attr(df, "traktr_aoi"): an sf with two columns: .name (sequential AOI ID) and geometry.

  • attr(df, "traktr_aoi_params"): a list with list(method = "buffer", dist_m = dist, crs_planar = crs_planar, id_col = .name).

  • The input is also marked with class "traktr_df" for downstream verbs.

See also

mutate_aoi_h3, fetch_ndvi, fetch_landuse

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
df <- tibble::tibble(
  id  = 1:3,
  lon = c(8.54, 8.55, NA_real_),
  lat = c(47.37, 47.38, 47.39)
)

df <- mutate_aoi_buffer(
  df,
  lat = lat, lon = lon,
  dist = 100,
  .name = "aoi_id",
  crs_planar = 3857
)

# Inspect AOI IDs and polygons
df$aoi_id
attr(df, "traktr_aoi")
} # }
